The '''percent sign''' {{char|%}} (sometimes '''per cent sign''' in [[British English]]) is the symbol used to indicate a [[percentage]], a number or [[ratio]] as a [[fraction (mathematics)|fraction]] of 100. Related signs include the [[permille]] (per thousand) sign {{char|‰}} and the [[Basis point#Permyriad|permyriad]] (per ten thousand) sign {{char|‱}}. Higher proportions use [[parts-per notation]].

== Correct style ==

=== Form and spacing ===
English style guides prescribe writing the percent sign following the number without any space between (e.g. 50%).<ref>{{multiref2
|1= {{cite news |title= Guardian and Observer style guide: P |work= [[The Guardian]] |date= 30 April 2021 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-observer-style-guide-p |access-date= 2023-03-16 |archive-date= 28 December 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191228192202/http://www.theguardian.com/guardian-observer-style-guide-p |url-status= live }}
|2= {{cite web |title= The Chicago Manual of Style |publisher= [[University of Chicago Press]] |date= 2003 |url= http://www.chicagomanualofstyle.org/ |access-date= 2007-01-05 |archive-date= 5 January 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090105172745/http://www.chicagomanualofstyle.org/ |url-status= live }}
|3= {{cite book |title= Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association |date= 1994 |location= Washington, D.C. |publisher= American Psychological Association |page= 114 }}
|4= {{cite book |title= Merriam-Webster's Manual for Writers and Editors |date= 1998 |location= Springfield, Massachusetts |publisher= Merriam-Webster |page= 128 }}
|5= {{cite book |last1= DeRespinis |first1= Francis |last2= Hayward |first2= Peter |last3= Jenkins |first3= Jana |last4= Laird |first4= Amy |last5= McDonald |first5= Leslie |last6= Radzinski |first6= Eric |date= 2012 |orig-year= 2011 |title= The IBM Style Guide: Conventions for Writers and Editors |location= Boston |publisher= Pearson Education |page= 162 }}
|6= {{cite book |last= Covey |first= Stephen R. |date=  |title= FranklinCovey Style Guide: For Business and Technical Communication |location= Salt Lake City |publisher= FranklinCovey |page= 287 }}
|7= {{cite book |last= Dodd |first= Janet S. |date= 1997 |title= The ACS Style Guide: A Manual for Authors and Editors |location= Washington, D.C. |publisher= American Chemical Society |page= 264 }}
}}</ref> However, the [[International System of Units]] and [[ISO&nbsp;31-0]] standard prescribe a space between the number and percent sign,<ref>{{cite web
  | title = SI Brochure
  | publisher = [[International Bureau of Weights and Measures]]
  | year = 2006
  | url = http://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section5-3-7.html
  | access-date = 2016-05-05
  | archive-date = 21 March 2019
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190321011300/https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section5-3-7.html
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web
  | title = The International System of Units
  | publisher = [[International Bureau of Weights and Measures]]
  | year = 2006
  | url = http://www.bipm.org/utils/common/pdf/si_brochure_8.pdf
  | access-date = 2007-08-06
  | archive-date = 13 March 2020
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200313143915/https://www.bipm.org/utils/common/pdf/si_brochure_8.pdf
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web
  | title = Quantities and units – Part 0: General principles
  | publisher = [[International Organization for Standardization]]
  | date = 1999-12-22
  | url = http://www.iso.org/iso/en/CatalogueDetailPage.CatalogueDetail?CSNUMBER=3621
  | access-date = 2007-01-05
  | archive-date = 29 May 2007
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070529115226/http://www.iso.org/iso/en/CatalogueDetailPage.CatalogueDetail?CSNUMBER=3621
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref> in line with the general practice of using a [[non-breaking space]] between a [[numerical value]] and its corresponding [[unit of measurement]].

Other languages have other rules for spacing in front of the percent sign:
* In [[Basque language|Basque]], the percent sign is placed before the number and is spaced.<ref>{{cite web |title=ehuneko (%) - Euskara Batuaren Eskuliburua |url=https://www.euskaltzaindia.eus/index.php?option=com_ebe&view=bilaketa&Itemid=1161&task=bilaketa&id=467 |publisher=Academy of the Basque Language |access-date=17 September 2026 |language=eu}}</ref>
* In [[Czech language|Czech]] and in [[Slovak language|Slovak]], the percent sign is spaced with a non-breaking space if the number is used as a noun.<ref>{{cite web
  | title = Internetová jazyková příručka
  | trans-title = Internet language guide
  | language = cs
  | publisher = Ústav pro jazyk český Akademie věd ČR
  | year = 2014
  | url = http://prirucka.ujc.cas.cz/?id=880
  | access-date = 2014-11-24
  | archive-date = 14 February 2015
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150214110059/http://prirucka.ujc.cas.cz/?id=880
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref> In Czech, no space is inserted if the number is used as an adjective (e.g. "a 50% increase"),<ref>{{cite web
 |title       = Jazyková poradna ÚJČ AV ČR: FAQ
 |trans-title = Language Counseling Center of the Institute of Journalism of the Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic: FAQ
 |language    = cs
 |publisher   = Ústav pro jazyk český Akademie věd ČR
 |year        = 2002
 |url         = http://www.ujc.cas.cz/poradna/odpo.html#12st
 |access-date  = 2009-03-16
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20020419163402/http://www.ujc.cas.cz/poradna/odpo.html#12st
 |archive-date = 2002-04-19
}}</ref> whereas Slovak uses a&nbsp;non-breaking space in this case as well.<ref>{{cite web
 |title        = Jazyková poradňa
 |trans-title  = Language counseling center
 |language     = sk
 |publisher    = Petit Press
 |year         = 2013
 |url          = http://www.ujc.cas.cz/poradna/odpo.html#12st
 |access-date   = 2019-10-26
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20090221135605/http://www.ujc.cas.cz/poradna/odpo.html#12st
 |archive-date = 2009-02-21
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref>
* In [[Croatian language|Croatian]], the percent sign is spaced<ref>{{Cite web |title= Znak za postotak |trans-title= Percent sign |url= http://pravopis.hr/pravilo/znak-za-postotak/85/ |website= Hrvatski pravopis. [[Institut za hrvatski jezik i jezikoslovlje]] |language= hr}}</ref> with a non-breaking space.
* In [[Finnish language|Finnish]], the percent sign is always spaced, and a [[Finnish noun cases|case suffix]] can be attached to it using the [[Colon (punctuation)|colon]] (e.g. {{lang|fi|50&nbsp;%:n kasvu}} {{gloss|an increase of 50%}}).<ref>{{cite web
  | title = Kielikello 2/2006
  | language = fi
  | publisher = Kotimaisten kielten keskus
  | website = kotus.fi
  | year = 2006
  | url = http://www.kielikello.fi/index.php?mid=2&pid=11&aid=1696
  | access-date = 2015-06-30
  | archive-date = 1 May 2015
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150501222450/http://www.kielikello.fi/index.php?mid=2&pid=11&aid=1696
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref>
* In [[French language|French]], the percent sign must be spaced with a non-breaking space.<ref>{{cite book |title= Guide des principales règles typographiques |trans-title= Guide to the main typographic rules |publisher= [[Université Joseph-Fourier]] |url= https://grenoble-sciences.ujf-grenoble.fr/sites/default/files/pdf/auteur/guidetypo.pdf |access-date= 8 June 2022 |language= fr }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last= André |first= Jacques |date= |title= Petites leçons de typographie |trans-title= Short typography lessons |url= http://jacques-andre.fr/faqtypo/lessons.pdf |location= Rennes |publisher= [[Institut de recherche en informatique et systèmes aléatoires]] |page= 34 |access-date= 8 June 2022 |language= fr }}</ref>
* According to the [[Real Academia Española]], in [[Spanish language|Spanish]], the percent sign should be spaced.<ref>{{cite web
  | title = El % se escribe separado de la cifra a la que acompaña
  | language = es
  | trans-title = The % is written separated from the figure to which it accompanies
  | publisher = Fundeu
  | website = fundeu.es
  | year = 2012
  | url = https://www.fundeu.es/recomendacion/el-se-escribe-separado-de-la-cifra-a-la-que-acompana-802/
  | access-date = 2021-11-24
  | archive-date = 24 November 2021
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211124144146/https://www.fundeu.es/recomendacion/el-se-escribe-separado-de-la-cifra-a-la-que-acompana-802/
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref> Despite that, in North American Spanish ([[Mexican Spanish|Mexico]] and the [[Spanish language in the United States|US]]), several style guides and institutions either recommend the percent sign be written following the number without any space between or do so in their own publications in accordance with common usage in that region.<ref>{{cite web
  | title = Normas particulares de estilo
  | language = es

  | publisher = Colegio de México

  | year = 2020
  | url = https://estudiosdegenero.colmex.mx/index.php/eg/normas_estilo#:~:text=Porcentajes.,detr%C3%A1s%20de%20la%20%C3%BAltima%20cifra
  | access-date = 2022-04-05
  | archive-date = 10 May 2022

  | url-status = live
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web

  | url-status = live
  }}</ref> 
* In [[Russian language|Russian]], the percent sign is rarely spaced, contrary to the guidelines of the GOST 8.417-2002 state standard.
* According to the [[Swedish Language Council]], the percent sign should be preceded by a space in [[Swedish language|Swedish]], as all other units.
* In [[German language|German]], the space is prescribed by the regulatory body in the national standard [[DIN 5008]].
* In [[Turkish language|Turkish]] and some other [[Turkic languages]], the percent sign precedes rather than follows the number, without an intervening space.
* In [[Persian language|Persian]] texts, the percent sign may either precede or follow the number, in either case without a space.
* In [[Arabic language|Arabic]], the percent sign follows the number; as Arabic is written from [[right to left]], this means that the percent sign is to the left of the number, usually without a space.
* In [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]], the percent sign is written to the right of the number, just as in English, without an intervening space. This is because numbers in Hebrew (which otherwise is written from right to left) are written from left to right, as in English.
*In [[Dutch language|Dutch]], the official rule ([[Bureau of Normalization|NBN]] Z 01-002) is to place a space between the number and the sign (e.g. {{lang|nl|een stijging van 50&nbsp;%}}), but most of the time, the space is missing (e.g. {{lang|nl|een stijging van 50%}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title= procentteken (spatie) |trans-title= Percent sign (space) |url= https://www.vlaanderen.be/taaladvies/procentteken-spatie |access-date= 2021-11-27 |website= www.vlaanderen.be|language=nl}}</ref>

== Evolution ==
Prior to 1425, there is no known evidence of a special symbol being used for percentages. The [[Italian language|Italian]] term ''per cento'', "for a hundred", was used as well as several different abbreviations (e.g. "per 100", "p 100", "p cento"). Examples of this can be seen in the 1339 arithmetic text (author unknown) depicted below.{{sfnp|Smith|1898|loc=p. 437}} The letter p with its [[descender]] crossed by a horizontal or diagonal stroke (to indicate abbreviation) [[Scribal abbreviation|conventionally stood]] for per, por, par, or pur in Medieval and Renaissance [[palaeography]].<ref>[http://inkunabeln.ub.uni-koeln.de/vdibProduction/handapparat/nachs_w/cappelli/capp317.html Letter p.] ({{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418131146/http://inkunabeln.ub.uni-koeln.de/vdibProduction/handapparat/nachs_w/cappelli/capp317.html |date=18 April 2009 }}) / Cappelli, Adriano: [http://inkunabeln.ub.uni-koeln.de/vdibProduction/handapparat/nachs_w/cappelli/cappelli.html Lexicon Abbreviaturarum] ({{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150508180936/http://inkunabeln.ub.uni-koeln.de/vdibProduction/handapparat/nachs_w/cappelli/cappelli.html |date=8 May 2015 }}). 2. verb. Aufl. Leipzig 1928. Wörterbuch der Abkürzungen: pp. 256–257.</ref>

:[[File:Percent sign in 1339.png|left|thumb|upright=1.8|alt=1339 arithmetic text|1339 arithmetic text in ''Rara Arithmetica'', p. 437]]{{clear}}

At some point, a scribe used the abbreviation ''pc'' with a tiny loop or circle (depicting the ending ''-o'' used in [[masculine ordinal|Italian ordinals]], as in {{lang|IT|primo}}, {{lang|IT|secondo}}; it is analogous to the English ''-th'' as in ''25th''). This appears in some additional pages of a 1425 text which were probably added around 1435.{{sfnp|Smith|1898|loc=pp. 439–440}}

:[[File:Percent sign in 1425.png|left|thumb|upright=1.3|1425 arithmetic text in ''Rara Arithmetica'', p. 440{{sfnp|Smith|1898|loc=p. 440}}]]{{clear}}

The ''pc'' with a loop eventually evolved into a horizontal fraction sign by 1650 (see below for an example in a 1684 text){{sfnp|Smith|1898|loc=p. 441}} and thereafter lost the ''per''.{{sfnp|Smith|1898|loc=p. 440}}

:[[Image:Percent sign in 1648.png|left|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=1684 arithmetic text|1684 arithmetic text in ''Rara Arithmetica'', p. 441]]{{clear}}

In 1925, D. E. Smith  wrote, "The [[Solidus (punctuation)|solidus]] form ([[File:Percentsign in Poor Richard font.png|20px|alt=A modern percentage sign, a diagonal line with a zero on either side]]) is modern."{{sfnp|Smith|1925|loc=Vol. 2, p. 250}}

== Encodings ==

=== Unicode ===
The [[Unicode]] code points are:
* {{unichar
| 0025 | Percent sign}} (HTML <code>&amp;#37;</code>, <code>&amp;percnt;</code><ref>HTML5 is the only version of HTML that has a named entity for the percent sign, see https://www.w3.org/TR/html4/sgml/entities.html ("The following sections present the complete lists of character entity references.") and https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/CR-html5-20140731/syntax.html#named-character-references ("percnt;").</ref>),
* {{unichar|FF05|fullwidth percent sign|nlink=Halfwidth and fullwidth forms}}
* {{unichar|FE6A|small percent sign|nlink=Small Form Variants}}
* {{unichar|066A|ARABIC PERCENT SIGN|html=}}, which has the circles replaced by square dots set on edge, the shape of the digit 0 in [[Eastern Arabic numerals]].
* {{unichar|332B|SQUARE PAASENTO}}, {{lang|ja|パーセント}} ({{Transliteration|ja|pāsento}}, from English "percent") in one square character.

=== ASCII ===
The [[ASCII code]] for the percent [[character (computing)|character]] is 37, or 0x25 in [[hexadecimal]].

== Other uses ==

=== In computers ===
Names for the percent sign include percent sign (in [[ITU-T]]), [[Modulo operation|mod]], grapes (in [[Hacker (programmer subculture)|hacker]] jargon),<ref>{{cite book|title=The New Hacker's Dictionary|edition=3rd|publisher=MIT Press|editor-first=Eric S.|editor-last=Raymond|editor-link=Eric S. Raymond|year=1996|isbn=9780262680929|page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=g80P_4v4QbIC&pg=PA45 45]}}</ref> and the humorous double-oh-seven (in [[INTERCAL]]).

In [[computing]], the percent [[character (computing)|character]] is also used for the [[modulo operation]] in [[programming language]]s that derive their syntax from the [[C (programming language)|C programming language]], which in turn acquired this usage from the earlier [[B (programming language)|B]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cm.bell-labs.com/cm/cs/who/dmr/kbman.html |title=Users' Reference to B |first=Ken |last=Thompson |year=1996 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060706005453/http://cm.bell-labs.com/cm/cs/who/dmr/kbman.html |archive-date=2006-07-06 }}</ref>

In the textual representation of [[Uniform Resource Identifier|URIs]], a {{code|%}} immediately followed by a 2-digit [[hexadecimal]] number denotes an octet specifying (part of) a character that might otherwise not be allowed in URIs (see [[percent-encoding]]).

In [[SQL]], the percent sign is a [[wildcard character]] in "LIKE" expressions, for example {{code|SELECT * FROM table WHERE fullname LIKE 'Lisa %'|sql}} will fetch all records whose names start with "{{mono|Lisa }}".

In [[TeX]] (and therefore also in [[LaTeX]]) and [[PostScript]], and in [[GNU Octave]] and [[MATLAB]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://octave.org/doc/interpreter/Single-Line-Comments.html#Single-Line-Comments|publisher=GNU|title=2.7.1 Single Line Comments|access-date=20 July 2018}}</ref> a {{code|%|lang=latex}} denotes a line [[comment (computing)|comment]].

In [[BASIC]], [[Visual Basic]], [[Active Server Pages|ASP]], and [[Visual Basic for Applications|VBA]] a trailing {{code|%}} after a variable name marks it as an [[integer]].

In [[Active Server Pages|ASP]], the percent sign can be used to indicate the start and end of the ASP code {{code|<%...... %>}}

In [[Perl]] {{code|%}} is the [[Sigil (computer programming)|sigil]] for [[Hash table|hashes]].

In many programming languages' string formatting operations (performed by functions such as <code>[[printf]]</code> and <code>[[scanf]]</code>), the percent sign denotes parts of the template string that will be replaced with arguments. (See [[printf format string]].) In [[Python (programming language)|Python]] and [[Ruby (programming language)|Ruby]] the percent sign is also used as the string formatting operator.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.python.org/2/library/stdtypes.html#string-formatting|title=Python 2 – String Formatting Operations|access-date=28 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#printf-style-string-formatting|title=Python 3 – printf-style String Formatting|access-date=28 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/String.html#method-i-25|title=Ruby – String#%}}</ref>

In the [[command processor]]s [[COMMAND.COM]] (DOS) and [[CMD.EXE]] (OS/2 and Windows), {{code|%1|lang=bat}}, {{code|%2|lang=bat}},&nbsp;... stand for the first, second, etc. parameters of a [[batch file]].  {{code|%0|lang=bat}} stands for the specification of the batch file itself as typed on the command line.  The % sign is also used similarly in the {{code|FOR|lang=bat}} command.
{{code|%VAR1%|lang=bat}} represents the value of an [[environment variable]] named {{code|VAR1}}. Thus:
{{code|2=bat|1=set PATH=c:\;%PATH%}}
sets a new value for {{code|PATH}}, that being the old value preceded by "<code>c:\;</code>".
Because these uses give the percent sign special meaning, the sequence {{code|%%|lang=bat}} (two percent signs) is used to represent a literal percent sign, so that:
{{code|2=bat|1=set PATH=c:\;%%PATH%%}}
would set {{code|PATH}} to the literal value "<code>c:\;%PATH%</code>".

In the [[C Shell]] and [[Z shell]], {{code|%}} is part of the default [[Prompt (computing)|command prompt]].

=== In linguistics ===
In linguistics, the percent sign is prepended to an example sentence or other [[String (computer science)|string]] to show that it is judged [[well-formedness|well-formed]] (grammatical) by some speakers and ill-formed by others. This may be due to differences in [[dialect]] or even individual [[idiolect]]s.<ref>{{Cite book | first=R. L. | last=Trask | author-link=Larry Trask | title=A Dictionary of Grammatical Terms in Linguistics | location=London | publisher=Routledge | year=1993 | isbn=0-415-08627-2 | page=203}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | first=David | last=Crystal | author-link=David Crystal | title=A Dictionary of Linguistics and Phonetics | edition=6th | location=Cambridge | publisher=Cambridge University Press | year=2008 | isbn=978-1-4051-5296-9 | page=355}}</ref> This use is similar to those of the [[Asterisk#Ungrammaticality|asterisk]] to mark ill-formed strings, the [[Question mark#Linguistics|question mark]] to mark strings where well-formedness is unclear, and the [[Number sign#Other uses|number sign]] to mark strings that are syntactically well-formed but semantically or pragmatically nonsensical.
